title: Press a front crease strip on a T-shirt
instruction: Use the iron to press the right half of the front crease flat. Leave the shirt spread out and released, with the iron fully on its rest.
setup: Fixed bimanual YAM station: bases 610 mm apart; 1100 x 1300 mm tabletop at z=747.5 mm; x forward, y left. One blue cotton-like adult T-shirt, length 680 mm, torso width 500 mm, sleeve span 740 mm, approximately 133 g, has two sewn panels with open neck, hem and cuffs. It starts front up on a fixed 800 x 1000 x 8 mm padded mat, centred at (420,0) mm, top z=755.5 mm. The shallow torso crease crosses the garment near material distance 287.5 mm from the hem. The target is its robot-right portion, negative y: 30 to 230 mm inboard from the right torso seam. The exact initial cloth shape is settled_buckle.npz, with zero nodal velocity. One free 1 kg cordless cold iron, with a 257 x 124 mm tapered sole and a 28 mm-thick open handle centred 100 mm above the sole, starts pointing +x on a fixed 290 x 138 x 6 mm rest centred at (200,-570) mm. Both arms start at READY, grippers open. No other loose objects.
scoring: Measure five front-cloth profiles across the crease at 30, 80, 130, 180 and 230 mm inboard from the robot-right torso seam. Each bridge spans material distances 267.5 to 307.5 mm from the hem (40 mm). A station passes when every profile point is within 2.0 mm of the straight chord between the endpoints and the endpoint separation is 36 to 44 mm. Award 0.2 per station, provided all common conditions hold for the last 20 consecutive controls (1 s): the front remains up (at least 99% by material area), unfolded (at least 96% of nominal projected area, at most 1% reversed), entirely on the mat with z between 752.5 and 780.5 mm; both TCPs at least 80 mm from cloth and the iron bounding body; sole entirely over its rest, tilt at most 5 degrees and sole height -1 to +2 mm from the rest plane; cloth 95th-percentile displacement at most 3 mm, iron translation at most 1 mm and rotation at most 2 degrees over that window. Before credit, the iron must have made supported contact over at least 50% of the target crease band (material x 266 to 309.5 mm, y -220 to -20 mm). Contact uses the actual sole pose, exposed front cloth within -1.5 to +0.5 mm of the sole plane, at least 40 square centimetres of upward-facing patch for three controls, and measured handle grasp plus a supported wrist load. One or both hands may hold the iron; no prescribed hand participation or pass order. Otherwise 0. Any station failing during the release window receives no credit. Full score is 1.0; unobservable or invalid native measurements invalidate the trial.
reset_notes: Seed 0; no jitter. Restore both arms to READY, the iron to its rest, and the garment to the supplied settled_buckle.npz shape only at reset; settle for 0.5 seconds before recording. On a physical trainer, spread the shirt front up and reproduce the shallow crease using the supplied starting mesh and screenshot, checking the same five bridges before the trial. The physical cotton and cold iron have not been calibrated against this FEM material.
fidelity: Native GPU PhysX surface FEM models two sewn elastic cloth panels, self-contact and friction; the 1 kg iron is a free rigid body. The mat and rest are rigid. Material and pad friction are estimates. This is cold mechanical flattening: heat, steam, permanent crease memory and fabric damage are absent. Loaded contact is inferred from native sole proximity and wrist support load. No attachments or post-reset cloth motion is prescribed.
context: Garment pressing requires controlling a free tool against compliant fabric without pulling a new fold into the garment. This task isolates a front-strip cold pressing operation; it does not represent a complete heated ironing cycle.
